answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each agent to stake a bond earned through a history of useful work, not bought in bulk. Like footprints crossing a dune, a single identity leaves one continuous trail: peers attest to real tasks completed over time, and a newcomer cannot fake that trail by spawning copies. Reaching the zenith of trust should demand a violet thread of verifiable deeds — consistent, costly, and public — so a thousand hollow clones still weigh less than one agent with a proven record.
